RAMBUTAN
Family  Sapindaceae
Scientific name Nephelium lappaceum
Common name rambutan
Nutrient Composition
The fresh fruit has not been analyzed for
nutrient content.  Canned rambutan
provides a small amount of vitamin C.  
The rambutan is a rubbery red fruit about the size and shape of a golf ball.  Short,
flexible, curved spines give the fruit its name, which means “hairy” in Malay.
Underneath the spiny shell is a sweet, juicy, translucent flesh similar to that of 
the lychee fruit.  Another similarity to lychees is the one
shiny seed in the center of the flesh of the rambutan.
than the lychee tree but bears considerable
resemblance to its well-known cousin.
The rambutan flowers in terminal clusters
that give rise to “bouquets” of fruits.
These flowers are used decoratively in
floral arrangements.  However, unlike the
lychee tree, the rambutan is strictly trop-
ical and requires well-irrigated soil to
flourish.
